say: pee-PAIR ehd-SEEK, or PIPE-er HIDE-sick in English

founded.what: The year a cloth merchant from Westphalia named Heidsieck founded the house in Reims, by the house's own account.

kind.means: A négociant manipulant, a house in the trade's own word: it buys grapes from growers across more than a hundred crus beyond any vines of its own and makes the wine itself.

story: Piper-Heidsieck dates itself from 1785, when a cloth merchant from Westphalia named Heidsieck, settled in Reims, began to make Champagne. The story the house tells is that he presented his wine to Queen Marie Antoinette (1755 to 1793) in that year, a legend it has kept at the heart of its name. His nephew later went into business with a partner called Piper, and in 1838, by the house's account, Piper married the widow of his late partner, and the two names came together as Piper-Heidsieck. In 1976 the house made the first vintage of Rare, a Chardonnay led prestige cuvée, and unveiled it at the Château de Versailles in 1985, with a jewelled edition by Van Cleef and Arpels. Rémy Martin bought the house in 1988, by the Rémy Cointreau group's own history, and on 8 July 2011 the group sold it to EPI, a family holding company, with Charles Heidsieck. In 2018 Rare became a house of its own, and the bottles stopped carrying the Piper-Heidsieck name. In September 2021 the house released Hors-Série 1971, a vintage held in its cellars for half a century, as the first of a new collection.

style.line: Pinot Noir led and fruit forward: a generous, open style built from many crus and steadied with reserve wines, with a drier Extra Brut range beside the Brut.
style.grapes: Pinot Noir leads, with Meunier and Chardonnay, drawn from more than a hundred crus across Champagne; Cuvée Brut is about half Pinot Noir, three tenths Meunier and a fifth Chardonnay, by the house.
style.reserve: Reserve wines steady the house style; the Essentiel sheets give 20 to 30 per cent reserve wines by the release, by the house, and no figure is given for Cuvée Brut.
style.lees: At least 36 months in the cellars for each Essentiel cuvée, by the house: the Brut's own figure was not found.
style.dosage: Extra Brut for the Essentiel range, by the house; 9 grams a litre for Rare 2013, by the importer's sheet.

nv.name: Cuvée Brut
nv.note: The non vintage Brut most guests know: about half Pinot Noir, with Meunier and a little Chardonnay, from more than a hundred crus, by the house.

cuvee.name: Rare Millésime

first.what: The first vintage, made by Piper-Heidsieck and unveiled at the Château de Versailles in 1985, by the house.

cuvee.rhythm: Made only in years the house declares, from the 1976 on. Its own pages have listed eleven, from 1976 to 2013, the 1998 the first in magnum, and trade accounts add a 1985 and a 2015.
cuvee.blend: Chardonnay leads, with Pinot Noir for the rest: about seven parts to three in the 2013, by its sheet, with no Meunier.
cuvee.sites: Eleven crus for the 2013, most of them in the Montagne de Reims: the Chardonnay from Villers-Marmery, Vaudemanges, Verzy, Ambonnay, Avize, Chouilly, Oger and Montgueux, in the Aube, the Pinot Noir from Verzy, Verzenay, Ambonnay, Bouzy and Tauxières.
cuvee.making: A vintage wine of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir, much of the Chardonnay from the Montagne de Reims, where Pinot Noir usually rules. For the 2013, by the importer's sheet: at least eight years on its lees, disgorged in December 2022, dosed at 9 grams a litre and rested at least a year under cork after disgorging. The vessels and the malolactic conversion were not found.
cuvee.lees: At least eight years for the 2013 by the importer's sheet; a British importer gives nine.
cuvee.bottle: For the 1976 vintage's unveiling at Versailles in 1985, Van Cleef and Arpels made a jewelled edition in gold, diamonds and lapis lazuli, by the house and a trade account.
cuvee.young: White peach, candied citrus peel and toasted almond, with the cool tension of Chardonnay grown in the Montagne de Reims and a long, fresh finish.
cuvee.aged: The house describes its 1988 as warm and generous, a wine to sip alone like a fine cognac, and gives its vintages decades of life, the 2008 to about 2050.

forms.name: Rare Rosé Millésime
forms.note: The vintage rosé of the same name, first made with the 2007 vintage, by the trade press.

cuvee.serve: 8 to 10 degrees Celsius, never ice cold; no need to decant; a tulip or a white wine glass.

also.name: Hors-Série

first.what: The vintage of the first release, disgorged in 2021 after half a century in the house's cellars and released that September.

also.note: What Piper-Heidsieck has made at the top of its range since Rare stood alone in 2018: a collection that revisits old vintages from the house's own cellars, not a wine made every declared year. The first, Hors-Série 1971, was Pinot Noir and Chardonnay in equal parts from Grand and Premier Cru villages, by the house and Decanter. Learn Rare as the class answer and Hors-Série as the name the house has used since 2021.
also.line: Since Rare became its own house, Piper-Heidsieck has released Hors-Série, old vintages from its cellars, beginning with a 1971 in 2021.

table.house45: Piper-Heidsieck is a house of Reims that dates itself from 1785. The house tells that its founder, a cloth merchant named Heidsieck, presented his wine to Marie Antoinette that year. Later a partner called Piper married into the family, in 1838, and the two names came together. The style is Pinot Noir led and generous, built from more than a hundred villages. Cuvée Brut is the bottle most guests know. For some forty years its prestige cuvée was Rare, first made in 1976, which became a house of its own in 2018.
table.house10: Piper-Heidsieck is the Reims house of 1785, Pinot Noir led and generous, where the prestige cuvée Rare was born in 1976.
table.cuvee45: Rare is the vintage Champagne that Piper-Heidsieck first made in 1976 and that has stood as a house of its own since 2018. It is made only in the years the house declares, never as a matter of course. Chardonnay leads, about seven parts to three with Pinot Noir. Much of that Chardonnay grows on the Montagne de Reims, the hill better known for Pinot Noir. Expect white peach, candied citrus peel and toasted almond. I serve it cool but not cold, in a white wine glass, so the fruit opens.
table.sale: If you would like a vintage Champagne with real rarity behind the name, Rare is made only in the years the house declares, Chardonnay led and long aged. May I bring a bottle for the table?
table.cuvee10: Rare is the Chardonnay led vintage Champagne born at Piper-Heidsieck in 1976, a house of its own since 2018.
table.cuvee20: Rare began in 1976 as the prestige cuvée of Piper-Heidsieck and became a house of its own in 2018. It is Chardonnay led, made only in declared years, with white peach, candied citrus peel and toasted almond.

guests.a: It was born there, first made with the 1976 vintage as the house's prestige cuvée. Since 2018 Rare has been a house of its own, and its bottles no longer carry the Piper-Heidsieck name.

guests.q: So which prestige cuvée does Piper-Heidsieck make since Rare left?
guests.a: The house has released Hors-Série, old vintages kept in its own cellars, beginning in 2021 with a 1971. For the class, the answer the sheet wants is Rare.

guests.q: Is Piper-Heidsieck the same as Charles Heidsieck?
guests.a: No. They are separate houses of Reims that were sold together to the same family holding company in 2011, and a third house, Heidsieck and Co Monopole, carries the name too.

traps: Three separate houses carry the name: Piper-Heidsieck, Charles Heidsieck and Heidsieck & Co Monopole.
Rare began as Piper-Heidsieck's prestige cuvée but has been its own house since 2018.
The class sheet prints Formerly Rare: Rare is the cuvée to name, and Formerly says it has not been Piper-Heidsieck's since 2018.
Rare is Chardonnay led although much of its fruit comes from the Montagne de Reims; Cuvée Brut, the house's non vintage, is Pinot Noir led.

sheet.label: Rare Millésime, and since 2021 Hors-Série for the house
sheet.note: The sheet's Formerly is not part of any label: it says Rare was Piper-Heidsieck's prestige cuvée before it became a house of its own in 2018. Answer Rare in class, and know Hors-Série as what the house has released since.

cards.front: Piper-Heidsieck: which prestige cuvée does the class sheet give it, and what does Formerly mean?
cards.back: Rare, first made in 1976; Formerly because Rare has been a house of its own since 2018. The house has since released Hors-Série.

cards.front: Rare, the Chardonnay led vintage Champagne: at which house was it born?
cards.back: Piper-Heidsieck, of Reims, with the 1976 vintage.

cards.front: What was the vintage of Piper-Heidsieck's first Hors-Série, and in which year was it released?
cards.back: The 1971, disgorged and released in 2021 after half a century in the house's cellars.

questions.q: The class sheet marks one Reims house's prestige cuvée as Formerly its own, the wine having become a house in 2018. Which cuvée is it?
questions.exp: Rare was Piper-Heidsieck's prestige cuvée from the 1976 vintage until it stood alone in 2018. Cristal is Louis Roederer's, Hemera is Henriot's and Celebris is Gosset's.

questions.q: From which year does Piper-Heidsieck date its founding?
questions.exp: Piper-Heidsieck dates itself from 1785, the year of its founder's legend at the court of Marie Antoinette. 1729 is Ruinart's year, 1772 Veuve Clicquot's and 1851 the year of Charles Heidsieck, a separate house.

questions.q: Which grape leads Rare, though much of its fruit grows on the Montagne de Reims?
questions.exp: Rare is Chardonnay led, about seven parts to three with Pinot Noir in the 2013, much of the Chardonnay from the Montagne de Reims. Pinot Noir leads the house's Cuvée Brut, and Meunier plays no part in the 2013.

report: Built on the library's p-piper-heidsieck and p-rare-champagne, contradicting neither; both library traps on Rare and the three Heidsiecks are kept word for word, and the year 2018 for Rare standing alone is the library's, which one trade account dates to September 2018.

The founder is described, not named: his dates, 1749 to 1828, were found on Wikipedia alone, and the Marie Antoinette meeting of 1785 is told as the house's legend; Piper's dates were not found either.
kind.code: the letters NM were not read on a label by the author; the refuter read NM 211 001 on a Brut label in the Open Food Facts database.

The cuvée's name: the house's own page heads it Rare Millésime, and newer bottles read Rare Champagne Millésime; the record uses Rare Millésime and the sheet's Formerly is explained in sheet, a trap and a card.

The plan's note that the house said it no longer had a prestige cuvée once Rare stood alone was not confirmed in any summary read, so the record says only that Hors-Série is what the house has released since; Decanter calls Hors-Série a new chapter, and one account calls it a limited edition prestige cuvée.
Hors-Série 1971: the 2,021 bottles of the release are left out, found in one account only; Decanter's 10 grams a litre and its twelve crus are left out too.

The vintages of Rare: the house's own pages list eleven, 1976 to 2013, and say it declares only exceptional years; a critic's list adds 1985 and 2015, which are left out because that source names a living critic and no second was found.

The bottle: the tiara the plan names was not confirmed (one search summary credits a tiara to Arthus-Bertrand, another to Van Cleef and Arpels), so only the jewelled edition of 1985 is told; the refuter cut the author's own clause on the gold work, which no source carried.
Style fields: vessels and malolactic are empty, no page read stating them; the reserve and lees figures are the Essentiel range's, Cuvée Brut's own being unfound.
The young glass is the library's own (white peach, candied citrus, toasted almond); no note of an aged bottle was sourced, so cuvee.aged says so.
Rare Rosé's first vintage, 2007, rests on the trade press of its 2016 launch, which also names a 2008; its blend was not sourced.

changed: story, table.house45: the two names joined on the label in 1838 became the names came together after the marriage of 1838, since one merchant dates the label name to 1845.
story: Rare was given a name and a house of its own became Rare became a house of its own, in 2018.
cuvee.bottle: the author's clause on the gold work cut, as no source carries it; the 1985 jewelled edition confirmed by a trade account.
cuvee.rhythm: the eleven vintages told as what the house's pages listed, with the 1985 and 2015 added from trade accounts; table.cuvee45 no longer counts them.
kind.code: NM read on a Brut label (NM 211 001, Open Food Facts); the report says so.
open: The 1985 and 2015 vintages rest on trade accounts, not on the house's own list as the author read it.
The founder's dates (1749 to 1828) stand on Wikipedia alone, so he stays described.
Hors-Série 1971's 2,021 bottles now have two trade accounts (Wine Industry Advisor, a Luxembourg trade page) but are still left out as a figure that serves no question.
Vessels and malolactic were not found by this refuter either.
